negative_findings.result_summary: Addiko's Slovenian subsidiary appears to disclose only through the Vienna-listed group (addiko.com), where Slovenia is a reporting segment. Country-level branch/ATM/card detail must therefore be extracted from group segment reporting rather than a local report.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Slovenia-specific card and network metrics for Addiko may be thinner and less granular than for NLB/OTP/Intesa, so segment-report extraction plus locator scraping is the fallback.

negative_findings.description: No FY2025 annual report was located for NLB in this pass; the newest NLB annual reports surfaced were FY2023 (sl and en), alongside a Q1 2026 investor news item and the May 2026 Investor Day page.
negative_findings.result_summary: Search indexing appears to lag the issuer's own IR index. This is an indexing/recency gap, not evidence that FY2024/FY2025 reports do not exist — the IR index pages must be crawled directly rather than relied on via search.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection design must crawl issuer IR indexes on a schedule instead of depending on search engines, or the latest network/card figures will be missed by a year or more.

negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any branch/ATM/card time series across 2024 has a structural break and double-counting risk; legacy domains should be archived before they are retired.

negative_findings.description: No machine-readable (API/CSV/JSON) disclosure of ATM fleet size, branch count or cards-in-issue was found for any Slovenian private bank in this pass; all such figures sit inside narrative PDF annual reports or on HTML locator pages.

negative_findings.why_it_matters: Sets realistic expectations on extraction cost and error rates for this cell; argues for a locator-endpoint reconnaissance task.

coverage_gaps.description: All URLs in this slice come from search-result metadata; none were fetched and confirmed reachable in this pass, and several deep PDF paths (year-foldered NLB, ISP, OTP downloadfile ids) are of the kind that rotate.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run the deterministic liveness pass over every candidate; on 404 re-derive from the issuer index page rather than marking dead, and on 403/timeout retry with browser-like headers.

coverage_gaps.description: Bank sustainability/ESG reports, Pillar 3 disclosures beyond Gorenjska banka and Sparkasse, and AJPES JOLP (public filed annual accounts) were not systematically searched, though AJPES is the statutory repository where every Slovenian bank files.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a dedicated pass on AJPES JOLP for filed annual reports of all licensed banks and savings banks, plus each bank's razkritja/Pillar 3 page; both give comparable structured filings independent of issuer web design.

coverage_gaps.description: Foreign-bank branches and niche private issuers in Slovenia (e.g. BKS Bank AG branch, N Banka wind-down legacy, Deželna banka Slovenije, UniCredit Banka Slovenija) were not covered in this pass; DBS and UniCredit in particular are material card/ATM issuers.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Extend the actor map from the Banka Slovenije register subjektov nadzora and the ZBS member list, then run the same letno-porocilo/bankomati/kartice query template against each missing actor.

coverage_gaps.description: Branch/ATM locator pages were classified as indirect sources on reasoning, but their backing data endpoints, robots.txt posture and record counts were not inspected.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Reconnaissance task: for nlb.si, otpbanka.si, intesasanpaolobank.si and dh.si locators, identify the JSON/map API, count records, and check robots.txt/ToS to establish whether periodic counting is permissible.

coverage_gaps.description: The cell rationale assumes private banks bypass public procurement portals, but bank-to-vendor relationships for ATM hardware, card personalisation and processing (e.g. Bankart as the shared national processor) are not visible in the sources gathered here.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Handle in a processor/vendor-focused cell: annual reports name shared infrastructure providers, and those providers' own disclosures can reveal fleet and card volumes the banks omit.

brief: For Slovenia's private banks the disclosure landscape is bimodal: two listed issuers (NLB on LJSE/LSE, Addiko Bank AG on Vienna) publish rich, quarterly, English-language investor material with explicit network, card and ATM-fee commentary, while everyone else — OTP banka (the merged Nova KBM + SKB), Intesa Sanpaolo Bank, Gorenjska banka, Delavska hranilnica, Sparkasse, LON, Primorska hranilnica — discloses only through Slovenian-language letno porocilo PDFs on their own sites, typically with a 'poslovna mreza' section carrying branch, ATM and card figures. Local-language querying was essential: 'letno porocilo', 'poslovna mreza', 'bankomati', 'karticno poslovanje' and 'javne objave' surfaced the PDF archives that English queries never returned. Two structural cautions dominate: the 22 August 2024 Nova KBM/SKB merger breaks every network and card time series and puts the skb.si archive at risk of retirement, and no bank in this cell publishes machine-readable network data, so collection means scheduled PDF extraction plus branch/ATM locator scraping as an independent cross-check. Nothing in this slice was fetch-verified — every URL is a search-derived candidate awaiting the deterministic liveness pass.
